extracted.intended_audience: news editors and general newspaper readers
extracted.subtask_description: Writing and editing short wire-service news briefs and leads for publication on news homepages and front sections; includes datelines, bylines, sourcing and concise factual paragraphs that situate events and policy implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dateline and date
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a clear dateline with city and date (e.g., 'MARCH 29 (AP)-KEFLAVIK', 'LOMARCH 29 (AP)').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Datelines identify where and when the dispatch originated and signal timeliness. The file shows multiple datelines (city names and 'MARCH 29 (AP)') attached to individual briefs; keep them at the top of the story for reader/context and newsroom tracking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong lead summarizing the main fact
rubrics_metrics.description: Start with a concise lead that states the principal fact or development (example headings: 'AMS BUDGET cut LEAD ICELAND', 'NIGHT LEAD RED TRADE').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wire leads should name key actors, actions and the core news immediately (who, what, where). The page contains numerous short leads and night leads—use similar economy so editors can pick up the essential fact quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution to sources and officials
rubrics_metrics.description: Attribute claims and assertions to named sources (e.g., 'dispatches said', 'The State Department said today', 'official dispatches', reporter bylines).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The copy repeatedly uses attributions to 'dispatches', 'officials', and named spokesmen (Lincoln White, Secretary of Defense Wilson). Always specify the source of claims—especially for sensitive or interpretive statements—and include titles where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Byline and reporter credit
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a byline with the reporter's name and, where applicable, affiliation (e.g., 'BY WARREN ROGERS JR', 'BY TOM OCHILTREE').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wire stories carry reporter credit. Place bylines prominently so editors and readers can identify the author of a dispatch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use-of-copy timing/embargo labels (ADVANCE/for-use tags)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mark stories with release or advance-use instructions when necessary (example: 'ADVANCE FOR USE AT 7 P.M.EST THURSDAY MARCH 29').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing tags coordinate distribution and publication across time zones or embargoes. Maintain the exact instruction line to avoid premature publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neutral, factual tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain objective, non-editorial language—report facts and quotations without opinionated adjectives or advocacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The wire copy is written in a neutral register (reporting committee testimony, official worries, Soviet broadcasts). Preserve balance and avoid loaded or speculative phrasing unless attributed to a source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concise paragraphs and wire structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Write in short, punchy paragraphs suitable for scanning; separate discrete facts and quotes into their own short paragraphs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page uses very short paragraphs and sectional breaks (codes and brief items). This improves legibility for editors and for quick front-page cutting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Context and background inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide brief contextual background or historical details that explain the significance (examples on page: 1951 treaty history, U.S. spending on Icelandic defenses, prior budget testimony).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include only essential background that helps readers understand why the item matters—past treaties, precedents, prior votes, or budget figures—keeping background compact and directly relevant to the lead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of direct quotes for key positions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use quoted language to record officials' views verbatim (examples: 'I would not draw the quick conclusion', 'We do not intend to interfere in any way, shape or manner with the freedom of the press').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quotations should be exact and attributed. Use them to convey tone, denials, defenses and policy positions that can't be paraphrased without losing meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of authoritative figures and statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: Report concrete numbers, budget figures and statistics when available (e.g., defense budget totals, percentages of fish purchases, submarine counts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include authoritative numeric detail to substantiate claims, and attribute the source (committee testimony, officials). Round or clarify figures when original copy is garbled or unclear for publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newsroom/internal tracking codes and labels
rubrics_metrics.description: Include internal item codes and category labels used by the wire service (examples: 'A30WX (450)', 'A653', '30.24- 6001').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These codes assist distribution, priority and editorial routing. Preserve them in feeds so receiving editors can manage placement and sequence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Highlight policy and international implications
rubrics_metrics.description: Emphasize the broader policy or diplomatic significance of events (examples: NATO implications of Iceland's resolution, U.S.-Soviet reactions, budgetary impact on military posture).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wire copy should connect events to larger themes when relevant, briefly indicating potential consequences for alliances, budgets or legal/political outcomes so editors can assess news value.
